name: promptfoo
description: Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs. Red teaming/pentesting/vulnerability scanning for AI. Compare performance of GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more. Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration.  Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.
readmeHtml:
Promptfoo: LLM evals & red teaming

promptfoo is a CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps. Stop the trial-and-error approach - start shipping secure, reliable AI apps.

Website · Getting Started · Red Teaming · Documentation · Discord

Promptfoo is now part of OpenAI. Promptfoo remains open source and MIT licensed. Read the company update.

Quick Start

Requires Node.js >=22.22.0 for npm and npx usage. Node.js 24 LTS is recommended; see the runtime support guide.

npm install -g promptfoo
promptfoo init --example getting-started

Also available via brew install promptfoo and pip install promptfoo. You can also use npx promptfoo@latest to run any command without installing.

Most LLM providers require an API key. Set yours as an environment variable:

export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-abc123

Once you're in the example directory, run an eval and view results:

cd getting-started
promptfoo eval
promptfoo view

See Getting Started (evals) or Red Teaming (vulnerability scanning) for more.

What can you do with Promptfoo?

  • Test your prompts and models with automated evaluations
  • Secure your LLM apps with red teaming and vulnerability scanning
  • Compare models side-by-side (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Ollama, and more)
  • Automate checks in CI/CD
  • Review pull requests for LLM-related security and compliance issues with code scanning
  • Share results with your team

Here's what it looks like in action:

It works on the command line too:

It also can generate security vulnerability reports:

Why Promptfoo?

  • Developer-first: Fast, with features like live reload and caching
  • Private: LLM evals run 100% locally - your prompts never leave your machine
  • Flexible: Works with any LLM API or programming language
  • Battle-tested: Powers LLM apps serving 10M+ users in production
  • Data-driven: Make decisions based on metrics, not gut feel
  • Open source: MIT licensed, with an active community

  • CLI Usage

We welcome contributions! Check out our contributing guide to get started.

Join our Discord community for help and discussion.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A developer-centric CLI and library for evaluating LLM output quality, catching regressions, and optimizing prompts.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Promptfoo is a testing framework tailored specifically for large language models, allowing developers to define test cases, evaluate outputs against expected assertions, and systematically compare different models or prompt variations. It operates via a CLI or a Node.js library, integrating directly into existing CI/CD pipelines to catch LLM regressions before they reach production. Instead of relying on manual vibe checks, developers write deterministic or LLM-assisted assertions (like regex matches, exact string comparisons, or semantic similarity) to strictly grade AI responses. It provides a visual dashboard for comparing side-by-side prompt performance, making it easier to empirically tune system instructions and parameters.
keyFeatures: Deterministic and semantic assertions: Grade LLM outputs using strict regex patterns, exact matches, or AI-driven semantic similarity evaluations.
Matrix testing: Automatically evaluate multiple prompts across different models and variables in a single test run.
CI/CD integration: Natively hooks into GitHub Actions and other CI pipelines to block merges if prompt quality regresses.
Visual comparison dashboard: Generates a local web interface to visually inspect and compare test results side-by-side.
Provider agnostic: Supports querying OpenAI, Anthropic, local models via Ollama, and custom API endpoints directly.

useCases.title: Regression Testing for Prompts
useCases.description: Engineering teams run automated suites on every pull request to ensure changes to a system prompt do not break expected AI behaviors.

useCases.title: Model Migration Evaluation
useCases.description: Developers use matrix testing to empirically compare the cost and quality of switching from GPT-4 to a smaller open-source model like Llama 3.

useCases.title: Prompt Engineering Optimization
useCases.description: Prompt engineers systematically iterate on complex system instructions, using the visual dashboard to spot where specific edge cases fail.

useCases.title: Red Teaming Automation
useCases.description: Security researchers automate the injection of adversarial prompts to measure how robust a production LLM system is against jailbreaks.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Promptfoo is designed for software engineers, prompt engineers, and AI product managers who need to bring software engineering rigor to LLM applications. Users should be comfortable working in the terminal and defining configuration files in YAML or JSON.
